Take this free CAT Functions and Graphs online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Functions & Graphs chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Functions & Graphs tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Functions & Graphs

Domain and range, composition of functions, even/odd functions, modulus and greatest-integer functions and reading graphs.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • 1/√g(x) needs g(x) > 0; log g(x) needs g(x) > 0.
  • Even: f(−x) = f(x); Odd: f(−x) = −f(x).
  • (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)).
  • A function is invertible iff it is one-one and onto.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring domain restrictions from square roots and logs.
  • Reversing the order in composition.
  • Confusing |x| (range ≥ 0) with x.

quiz.title: CAT Functions & Graphs Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If f(x) = x/(x + 1) for x ≠ −1, then f(f(f(x))) equals:
The range of f(x) = (x² + x + 1)/(x² − x + 1) for all real x is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Let y = (x²+x+1)/(x²−x+1). Cross-multiply: y(x²−x+1) = x²+x+1.
Step 2: x²(y−1) − x(y+1) + (y−1) = 0. Discriminant ≥ 0: (y+1)² − 4(y−1)² ≥ 0.
Step 3: −3y² + 10y − 3 ≥ 0 → (3y−1)(y−3) ≤ 0 → 1/3 ≤ y ≤ 3.
Step 4: Both endpoints are achieved (y=1/3 at x=−1, y=3 at x=1).
Answer: [1/3, 3]

questions.q: The number of real solutions to |x² − 4| = x + 2 is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Case 1 (x²≥4, i.e. x≤−2 or x≥2): x²−4 = x+2 → x²−x−6=0 → (x−3)(x+2)=0 → x=3 or x=−2 (both valid). ✓✓
Step 2: Case 2 (−2 x<2): 4−x² = x+2 → x²+x−2=0 → (x+2)(x−1)=0 → x=1 (valid, since −2<1<2). ✓
Step 3: Total: 3 real solutions: x = −2, 1, 3.
Answer: 3

questions.q: For f(x) = x + ⌊x⌋, the range of f on x ∈ [0, 1) is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For x ∈ [0, 1), ⌊x⌋ = 0.
Step 2: f(x) = x + 0 = x.
Step 3: As x ranges over [0, 1), f(x) ranges over [0, 1).
Answer: [0, 1)

questions.q: If f satisfies f(x + y) = f(x)·f(y) for all real x, y, with f(0) ≠ 0, then f(0) equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set x = y = 0: f(0+0) = f(0)·f(0) → f(0) = [f(0)]².
Step 2: f(0)[f(0) − 1] = 0 → f(0) = 0 or f(0) = 1.
Step 3: Since f(0) ≠ 0, we must have f(0) = 1.
Answer: 1

questions.q: The range of f(x) = (x² + 2)/(x² + 1) for all real x is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write f(x) = 1 + 1/(x²+1). Since x²+1 ∈ [1,∞), 1/(x²+1) ∈ (0, 1].
Step 2: f(x) ∈ (1, 2]. At x=0: f=2 (maximum, achieved). As x→∞: f→1 (not reached).
Answer: (1, 2]

questions.q: If f: R → R satisfies f(xy) = xf(y) + yf(x) for all x, y ∈ R, then f(0) equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set x = y = 0: f(0) = 0·f(0) + 0·f(0) = 0 + 0 = 0.
Step 2: f(0) = 0 is the only possibility.
Answer: 0

questions.q: The number of real solutions to 2ˣ + 3ˣ = 5ˣ is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Divide both sides by 5ˣ: (2/5)ˣ + (3/5)ˣ = 1.
Step 2: At x = 1: 2/5 + 3/5 = 1. ✓ So x = 1 is a solution.
Step 3: Let g(x) = (2/5)ˣ + (3/5)ˣ. Since both terms are strictly decreasing in x, g is strictly decreasing. Hence exactly one solution.
Answer: 1

questions.q: Among integers n with −5 ≤ n ≤ 5, how many satisfy ⌊n/2⌋ = n/2?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: ⌊n/2⌋ = n/2 exactly when n/2 is an integer, i.e., when n is even.
Step 2: Even integers from −5 to 5: −4, −2, 0, 2, 4 → five values.
Answer: 5

questions.q: The number of distinct real roots of f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ + 4x² − 1 is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write f(x) = (x²−2x)² − 1 = (x²−2x−1)(x²−2x+1) = (x²−2x−1)(x−1)².
Step 2: x²−2x−1=0 → x = 1 ± √2. Two real roots.
Step 3: (x−1)²=0 → x=1. One distinct root.
Step 4: Distinct roots: 1−√2, 1, 1+√2 → 3 distinct real roots.
Answer: 3

faq.q: How do I find a domain quickly?
faq.a: Set denominators ≠ 0, expressions under even roots ≥ 0, and log arguments > 0, then take the intersection.
Exactly when it is one-one (injective) and onto (surjective) on its stated domain and codomain.
